history_note: T0054 is PRESERVED BYTE-FOR-BYTE and is not rewritten, and neither is any earlier receipt. defect.statement: T0054 records that pull request #13 was MERGED TO MASTER, and carries a timestamp 311 seconds EARLIER than the merge it records. A receipt asserting an event it pre-dates is not evidence of that event, and for 311 seconds the document asserted a merge that had not happened.

authoritative_sources.agreement_note: GitHub's merged_at and the merge commit's committer date are identical to the second, for this merge and for the Phase-4 merge before it. That is what makes the rule checkable from the repository alone, with no network call and no API token: the merge commit named inside a receipt carries the authoritative time.

defect.why_it_passed_every_existing_check: tools/validate-transition-times.sh bounded a receipt only from ABOVE -- a timestamp may not be later than the commit that INTRODUCED the file. T0054 satisfied that comfortably. Nothing compared a receipt against the event it DESCRIBES, so a merge receipt could be dated arbitrarily early and still pass.
defect.what_is_NOT_affected: Only the recorded timestamp is wrong. Every substantive claim in T0054 is unchanged and remains verified: the merge commit, its two parents, the tree-equality proof, the pre-merge conditions, the check runs, and the nine preserved limitations.

authoritative_merge_record.tree_equality_proof: master's tree after the merge is 1ed4c590172a8d7036eefaf245100ad73a263daa, byte-identical to the accepted head's tree, with zero paths differing. Unchanged by this correction.

governance_strengthened.rule: A receipt that records a pull-request merge may not be dated BEFORE the merge it records. The authoritative time is the committer date of the merge commit the receipt itself names, which equals GitHub's merged_at. A receipt whose record_type says a pull request was merged MUST name its merge commit; without one it is unfalsifiable and is refused rather than skipped. Equality is accepted -- a receipt stamped at exactly the merge time is not describing the future.
governance_strengthened.implemented_in: tools/validate-transition-times.sh (second rule, alongside the existing cannot-be-later-than-its-introducing-commit rule)
governance_strengthened.grandfathered: T0054 only, listed explicitly with its measured 311s discrepancy, printed on every run. The rule is enforced for every merge receipt written from this point on.
governance_strengthened.counter_proof: tools/validate-merge-receipt-times-selftest.sh drives the REAL validator -- never a copy -- with the grandfather list emptied, against real historical data rather than invented fixtures: T0054 must FAIL with its exact 311s discrepancy named, and T0048 (the Phase-4 merge receipt, written 17 seconds AFTER its merge) must PASS. Without the second case the first would also pass for a validator that refuses every merge receipt ever written. It further proves that equality is not treated as early, that a merge receipt naming no merge commit is refused as unfalsifiable, and that on the real ledger T0054 is reported as a visible grandfathered exception rather than silently skipped. 5/5.
